bull_bear.body: Prioritizing capex for high-margin product capacity and Cenexi integration; maintaining strong balance sheet (₹33,591 Cr cash); no dividend policy mentioned; reinvestment in R&D (5% of revenue) and CDMO pipeline
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: CDMO contract approvals delayed by regulators; Cenexi ramp-up slower than expected; currency volatility; supply chain disruptions; competitive pricing pressure in US
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident, disciplined, and forward-looking; emphasized sustained margin expansion, operational leverage, and Cenexi’s turnaround as core to strategy; avoided giving CDMO revenue guidance due to regulatory uncertainty
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Cenexi’s EBITDA positivity is structural, not cyclical — driven by fixed cost absorption from new lines and contract renegotiations; CDMO contracts are multi-year, high-margin, and locked in before commercialization; Gland is effectively becoming a single platform with Cenexi for global complex injectables
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Net-cash balance sheet: total cash and bank balances of Rs 35,466 Mn and net cash of Rs 32,939 Mn at Jun'26, versus Rs 25,562 Mn / Rs 22,870 Mn at FY25 (FY25 figures marked as excluding non-callable deposits of INR 3,960 million); net cash is defined as cash and cash equivalents less total borrowings including current maturities.
- Net worth (equity share capital plus other equity) of Rs 106,762 Mn at Jun'26, versus Rs 103,580 Mn at FY26 and Rs 91,507 Mn at FY25.
- Returns trending up on the deck's own definitions: RoCE 9% (FY25) to 11% (FY26) to 14% (Jun'26); RoNW 8% (FY25) to 11% (FY26) to 12% (Jun'26).
- Working-capital cycle shortening: cash conversion cycle of 172 days (FY25), 164 days (FY26) and 155 days (Jun'26), comprising receivable days 94, inventory days 122 and payable days 61 at Jun'26.
- Asset turnover as disclosed: total asset turnover 0.5x (FY25), 0.5x (FY26), 0.6x (Jun'26); fixed asset turnover 1.4x (FY25), 1.5x (FY26), 1.6x (Jun'26).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: US: ₹9,716 Cr Q4 (+26% YoY), 31 launches FY26; Europe & other regulated: ₹794 Cr Q4 (+11% YoY); Rest of World: ₹1,468 Cr Q4 (+17% YoY); India: ₹670 Cr Q4; Cenexi: €45 Mn Q4 (+4% YoY), EBITDA positive; CDMO: 46% of revenue, 33% growth, 23% of base revenue
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- Two business models of near-equal size in Q1 FY27: CDMO revenue of Rs 8,915 Mn and B2B revenue of Rs 9,088 Mn (B2B including B2C revenue of INR 152 Mn), on total revenue from operations of Rs 18,003 Mn; the deck's revenue-distribution chart shows a 50%/50% CDMO-B2B split for Q1 FY27.
- Geographic contribution to Q1 FY27 revenue as labelled by the deck: US 54%, Europe 22%, Rest of the World 17%, India 4% and Other Core Markets (Canada, Australia and New Zealand) 3%.
- Deep US registration base: cumulative 389 ANDA filings in the U.S., of which 342 are approved and 47 pending; the deck notes the ANDA count includes technology transfer ANDAs.
- Growth attribution the deck gives for its largest market, the US: CDMO driven by recent product launches (Dalbavancin and Multi-Vitamin), and B2B by volume expansion in existing products including Enoxaparin, Vancomycin, Chlorothiazide and Heparin.
- Europe growth attributed to volume expansion in existing products including Daptomycin and Cenexi CDMO products, plus the recent Dalbavancin launch.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Weak geography] Other Core Markets (Canada, Australia and New Zealand), 3% of Q1 FY27 revenue, saw revenue degrowth of -28% YoY, which the deck attributes to volume decline in the existing products.
- [India mix] India (4% of Q1 FY27 revenue) grew 12% YoY, with the deck attributing growth to CDMO for certain products including Huminsulin and a decline in B2B to lower sales of Enoxaparin.
- [RoW drivers] Rest of the World (17% of Q1 FY27 revenue) grew 2% YoY, with growth seen across some key products including Heparin, Huminsulin and Rocuronium Bromide.

deepdive.thesis: Strong Q4FY26 performance driven by 22% revenue growth and 30% EBITDA margin, fueled by new product launches (Dalbavancin, Multivitamin) and CDMO expansion, with full-year EBITDA margin rising to 26% and Cenexi turning EBITDA-positive; what matters is the sustained margin expansion from high-value products and Cenexi’s path to mid-teens EBITDA, positioning Gland as a global complex injectables leader.

open.item: New prefilled syringe line at Herouville on track to be operational at the beginning of CY2026; two new lyophilizers at Braine-l'Alleud to be qualified by end of CY2025.
Biologics business (Dr. Reddy's) expected to contribute ~INR100 crores in FY26, gradually increasing thereafter.
CMS dry powder variation filings pending in European countries with approval expected in ~6 months, providing potential upside to guidance if faster.
Preparing to replace an old ampoule line at Fontenay this summer with a new high-capacity line adding 30 million ampoule capacity by 2027.
Dalbavancin (approved Feb, launched US and Europe) and multivitamin portfolio (approved April) expected to be meaningful contributors to growth in FY27 and beyond.
Management expects EBITDA margins to remain strong going forward, supported by high-end launches, product ramp-ups and CDMO execution.
Next-year (FY27) capex expected to be more than INR400 crores as part of the 5-year INR2,000 crore program.
15 products advanced into co-development (seven 505(b)(2) filings and eight ANDAs) are expected to commercialise from FY 2027-28 onwards.
The major CDMO (oncology) project announced earlier progressing well, expected to be commercialized in H2 FY28 with estimated annual revenue potential of USD25-30 million.
Reaffirmed capex outlay of INR2,000 crores over the next five years to fund capacity expansions for existing products and planned new launches.
Cenexi reaffirmed its mid-term objective of achieving a mid-teen EBITDA margin, supported by capacity increases and a fast-growing business pipeline.
Expand cartridge fill-and-finish capacity to 140 million units per year (from ~40 million) to capitalise on the GLP-1 opportunity.
The Board has recommended a final dividend of Rs 20 per equity share for FY 2025-26, subject to shareholder approval.
An additional 11 Ready-to-Use (RTU) infusion bag products are currently under development, on top of 21 filed and 18 approved.
Three further in-house complex products are in line for approval, in addition to the six already launched.

open.horizon: at the earliest possible (no date stated)
open.item: Following the resignation of Chief Executive Officer Mr. Shyamakant Giri with effect from April 30, 2026, the Company states it will appoint a new Chief Executive Officer at the earliest possible.
Cenexi and Gland to increasingly operate as one unified platform, driving cross-selling and larger multi-geography contract wins.
Continuing to explore in-licensing opportunities in differentiated therapy areas and drug delivery systems like liposomals, biologics/biosimilars, plus capacity additions.
Cost initiatives (yield improvement, alternate sourcing, energy optimization, process efficiencies) continue to deliver approximately 1-2% margin improvement.
Commission new production lines at the Pashamylaram facility for suspensions.

verdicts.note: 'we have received approvals, particularly Dalbavancin in February... Dalbavancin has been launched in U.S. and European markets and is already seeing strong demand' - delivered, though later than the …

verdicts.item: Cenexi EBITDA breakeven pushed from Q4 FY25 to Q3 FY26, driven by pushing top line to a ~EUR50 million per quarter run rate, following lost production from the ANSM Fontenay inspection.
verdicts.note: 'After a profitable Q3 FY 26 quarter... we delivered an EBITDA of EUR1 million in Q4 FY 26' - breakeven achieved and sustained. [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: Reaffirmed medium-term goal of delivering positive EBITDA in full year 2026, driven by pushing revenue beyond the EUR200 million threshold.
verdicts.note: 'returned to profitability for the 3 quarters during the year'; FY26 revenue EUR182m - positive but below the EUR200m threshold. [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: 15 complex formulations under co-development with MAIA Pharmaceuticals (7 505(b)(2) and 8 ANDAs) with commercialization expected to begin from FY27.
verdicts.note: 'We also do co-develop projects, around 15 projects we are working with development partners' - the FY27 commercialization not specifically restated. [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: Cenexi targeted to reach high-teen EBITDA margins over the mid-to-long term (1-2 years).
verdicts.note: 'we are looking at mid-teen EBITDA level in the midterm'; FY27 target mid-single/high-single digit - approaching but below the original high-teen target.

verdicts.item: Guided GLP-1/cartridge fill-finish volumes to start at around 20 million units in FY27, ramping in subsequent years based on market approvals.
verdicts.note: 'the guidance we give is excluding GLP'; 'the ramp-up will happen mostly during that time' (post-2030) - the ~20m FY27 figure no longer emphasized. [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: After a to-be-expected low Q2 FY26 (summer shutdown), Cenexi committed to deliver positive EBITDA in Q3 FY26, EBITDA-positive from October, ramping to low-teens/high single digits.
